hero.headline: Automate Your eBay Store. Know Your Real Profit.
hero.subheading: SellerHill automates your Amazon-to-eBay workflow — listings, AI-optimized titles, price and stock sync, automatic orders, tracking updates and buyer messages. Then it shows your real profit from actual eBay net earnings and actual Amazon order costs.

p1.title: The automation you expect
p1.description: Listings, price and stock sync, automatic orders, tracking updates and buyer messages — the full Amazon-to-eBay workflow in one platform.

p2.title: A strategy per product group
p2.description: Setting Groups let you run different pricing rules, HTML templates and listing settings across different parts of your catalog.

p3.title: Real profit, not an estimate
p3.description: Your profit comes from the net earnings eBay actually paid you and the amount you actually paid on Amazon — not from an assumed margin.

features.sectionTitle: Everything You Need to Automate Your eBay Store
features.sectionSubtitle: The daily work of an Amazon-to-eBay store — listing, repricing, ordering, tracking and buyer communication — handled for you.

asinListing.title: AI-powered eBay listings
asinListing.description: Add an Amazon ASIN and SellerHill builds the eBay listing: product images, item specifics and an AI-optimized title.
asinListing.detail: Enter the Amazon ASINs you want to sell and SellerHill turns them into eBay-ready listings — product images, the item specifics buyers filter by, and a title optimized for eBay search with AI. Apply your own HTML listing template to control how the description looks.

priceStock.title: Automatic price & stock sync
priceStock.description: SellerHill checks your Amazon products about twice a day and updates your eBay listings when the price or availability changes.
priceStock.detail: SellerHill monitors the Amazon price and stock of every product you list, checking around twice a day. When something changes, your eBay listing is updated to match — so you are not selling an item that went out of stock, or holding a price that no longer leaves you a margin.

autoOrder.title: Automatic order fulfillment
autoOrder.description: When an eBay order comes in, SellerHill places the matching Amazon order and ships it to your buyer.
autoOrder.detail: Every eBay sale is turned into an Amazon order automatically and shipped to your buyer's address. You set a spending cap per buyer account, and any order that would go over it stops for your review instead of going through.

tracking.title: Automatic tracking updates
tracking.description: SellerHill follows the Amazon order, marks the eBay order shipped and uploads the tracking number.
tracking.detail: SellerHill monitors the Amazon order after it is placed. When it ships, the eBay order status is updated and the tracking number is uploaded to eBay — converted first when you have tracking conversion enabled, so your buyer sees a clean tracking number instead of your supplier.

buyerMessages.title: Automated buyer messages
buyerMessages.description: Order received, shipped, delivered and feedback request messages send themselves, using your own templates.
buyerMessages.detail: Set up messages for order received, shipped, delivered and feedback request. SellerHill sends each one at the right stage of the order using your own templates, so you never have to track who to contact and when.

multiStore.title: Multiple eBay stores
multiStore.description: Run several eBay stores from one account, each with its own settings, listings and reporting.
multiStore.detail: Manage more than one eBay store from a single SellerHill account. Each store keeps its own settings, listings, orders and profit reporting, and every screen can be filtered down to one store.

profit.sectionTitle: Revenue Isn't Profit. Know What You Actually Made.
profit.sectionSubtitle: SellerHill doesn't apply an estimated margin. It matches the net earnings eBay actually paid you with the amount you actually paid on Amazon, and reports what is left.

actuals.title: Actual numbers on both sides
actuals.description: The eBay net earnings come from the real sale. The order cost comes from the real Amazon order. Nothing in between is assumed.

confirmed.title: Confirmed profit
confirmed.description: Profit calculated from complete transaction data. This is the figure you can plan against.

estimated.title: Estimated profit
estimated.description: When cost data is still incomplete, the profit is labeled as an estimate and kept separate from your confirmed total.

pnl.title: Month-by-month P&L
pnl.description: Revenue, costs, margin and ROI across twelve months on one screen, exportable in a click.

panel.title: How a sale becomes profit
panel.formula: Actual eBay net earnings − actual Amazon order cost = real profit
panel.footnote: Only confirmed profit counts toward your headline figure. Estimates are shown separately, so you always know which numbers are final.

settingGroups.sectionSubtitle: Not every product should be priced or listed the same way. Create a Setting Group with its own pricing rule, HTML template and listing settings, then apply it to the products that need it. Build a strategy once and reuse it across your catalog.

howItWorks.sectionTitle: From ASIN to an Automated Store
howItWorks.sectionSubtitle: Set it up once, and the daily work stops being yours.

faq.sectionSubtitle: The things worth knowing before you start.

q1.question: How does automatic order fulfillment work?
q1.answer: When a buyer orders on eBay, SellerHill places the matching order on your connected Amazon account and ships it to the buyer's address. You set a spending cap per buyer account, and any order above that cap stops for your approval instead of going through.

q2.question: How often does price and stock sync run?
q2.answer: SellerHill checks the Amazon price and stock of your listed products about twice a day. When the price or availability changes, the matching eBay listing is updated in that cycle. This is scheduled monitoring, not real-time tracking.

q3.question: How does tracking automation work?
q3.answer: After the Amazon order is placed, SellerHill keeps monitoring it. When Amazon ships, the eBay order is marked shipped and the tracking number is uploaded to eBay, so your order is updated on time without you checking in on it.

q4.question: What is tracking number conversion?
q4.answer: An Amazon tracking number tells your buyer where the item came from. When conversion is enabled, SellerHill converts it into a different trackable number before uploading it to eBay. You choose whether conversion is on and which carriers it applies to.

q5.question: Can I customize the buyer messages?
q5.answer: Yes. Order received, shipped, delivered and feedback request each have their own template that you can edit, and you can turn any of the four on or off independently.

q6.question: How is real profit calculated?
q6.answer: SellerHill takes the net earnings eBay actually paid you for the sale — after eBay fees — and subtracts the amount you actually paid for the Amazon order, including tax and shipping. It compares two real transactions, rather than a selling price minus an estimated cost.

q7.question: What's the difference between confirmed and estimated profit?
q7.answer: Confirmed profit is calculated from complete transaction data on both sides. Estimated profit is shown while the cost data is still incomplete — for example before the Amazon order costs have been captured. Estimates are labeled and kept separate, so you always know which numbers are final.

q8.question: What are Setting Groups?
q8.answer: A Setting Group is a reusable set of listing settings — pricing rule, stock buffer, HTML template and other listing options. You create the group once and apply it to as many products as you like, instead of configuring each product separately.

q9.question: Can different product groups use different pricing and templates?
q9.answer: Yes, that is exactly what Setting Groups are for. Seasonal products can run a seasonal margin and template while your electronics run their own, and you can move products between groups at any time.

q10.question: Can I manage multiple eBay stores?
q10.answer: Yes. You can connect more than one eBay store to a single SellerHill account. Each store keeps its own settings, listings, orders and profit reporting, and you can filter every screen by store.

q11.question: Do I need to install any software?
q11.answer: No. SellerHill runs in the browser and connects to your accounts directly. There is no browser extension, no desktop app and nothing to keep running on your own machine.

q12.question: Can I try SellerHill before paying?
q12.answer: Yes, in two ways. The live demo opens the full application with sample data and needs no sign-up at all. Or create an account and start a 7-day free trial — no credit card required.
